passages.original: Αἰσχύλον ἥδε λέγει ταφίη λίθος ἐνθάδε κεῖσθαι
passages.english: This tomb-stone says that Aeschylus lies here
passages.notes: A single verse line, apparently the opening of an epitaph for Aeschylus; the sentence continues beyond the passage given.

passages.original: οὗ, κατὰ Πυθαγόρου φυσικὰν φάτιν, ἁ πρὶν Ὁμήρου
passages.english: whose [soul], according to Pythagoras' doctrine about nature, [which was] formerly Homer's
passages.notes: A fragmentary single line in Doric forms (φυσικὰν, ἁ). The feminine article ἁ evidently refers to a noun such as ψυχά (soul) in a following line, hence the supplied '[soul]'. The line alludes to Pythagorean transmigration: Homer's soul is said to live again in the person commemorated. The construction is incomplete within the passage, so the rendering is provisional.
